speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Michaelmas. Rent, Mistress Ansell, xx s., by noon. The almanac has it, and so do I. Sit down, the pair of you. The hall is where money is counted in this house.

speaker: michael_drayton
text: I came the short way, Will. Paul's was full of a wager, and I was not going to make you walk to it. Two writing-masters, before judges, for a pen of gold. A stall had the sheet pinned up. I brought you the sheet, since the hall is where you are.

speaker: michael_drayton
text: Would you enter?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It's the only prize-fight I could win, and then only if they judged by speed.

speaker: michael_drayton
text: Speed is a kind of praise. You are refusing the rest of the praise, which is wise. Their hands are secretary, chancery and italic on the one sheet. Yours, if you set it beside them, would look like hen-tracks, and the hen would be in a hurry.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Let the hen hurry. Fine handwriting is a neighbouring trade, and no more a proof of fine thinking than a good saddle is of a good horse.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: When the two of you have finished judging horses, there is twenty shillings to count. I will tell it once. Then I will tell it again. Noon is the bargain, and noon is not a poem.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Twenty shillings. Told twice. The quarter is paid, Master Shakespeare, and I will hear no wit about it until dinner has been survived.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It is paid, Mistress. I have no wit that would make it less, and I am not sorry to be quit of it.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: From today the firing and the washing are sixpence the week. I am naming the rate. I am not taking the coin. The first of it is not this noon. The first fire of the season is laid in your chamber. It is not lit. You may look at it, and you may not praise it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not praise a fire that has not been lit. Sixpence is the rate. I have heard it.

speaker: michael_drayton
text: He heard it twice, which is as near a vow as a poet comes on a Monday. Will, the sheet is yours to look at and not to keep, unless Mistress Ansell prefers it out of the house.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: The sheet can lie until I have shown him the loaf. In July I said that by Michaelmas we should be eating the board. Look at the notch.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: It wants a thumb and the breadth of a nail. I am letting the notch speak for itself. I have no sermon to add to a short loaf, and neither of you is to supply one.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The notch has spoken. I will not argue with bread.

speaker: michael_drayton
text: Nor I. A short loaf is a better argument than a golden pen, and cheaper to lose.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: One thing more, since the close will have told it by dinner if it has not told it already. It will not be Spencer. That is as much as this house knows, and this house is not going to invent the next name at my table.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then I will not invent it. The Mayor we have is enough Mayor for one week, and I did not come home to elect another.

speaker: michael_drayton
text: I heard the same in the street, and no name after it. I will not dress the news up. You have a king on Thursday. The City has a dinner. They are not the same appetite.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: His appetite is sops and a civil tongue. Yours, Master Drayton, is a cup if you want it, and the door when the cup is done. I am not boarding poets in pairs.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: He brought me a trade I do not practise. That is a neighbourly act. Let him have the cup, Mistress. I have already had the lesson about the saddle.

speaker: michael_drayton
text: I will drink to the saddle, then, and to speed, which is the only judge who would give you the pen. I should hate to see you win a contest for being neat. It would ruin you.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am in no danger of neatness. The playhouse hand is what it is. I am glad of the sheet, and I am gladder that the contest is not in this hall.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: The contest is over, for my purposes. The silver is in the box. The loaf is short. The fire upstairs is a promise and not a flame. When you have finished admiring a pen you did not win, one of you may move that sheet off my cloth.

speaker: michael_drayton
text: I will move it. Will is going to stare at it until the hands shame him, and shame is a slow meal.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Let me stare a minute more. A man should know what he is not, once a quarter, and Michaelmas will do for the date.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: One minute. Then the cloth is a cloth again. And you, Master Shakespeare, have a book to rule tonight. Do not rule it on this table while there is still bread on it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Tonight. Not on the bread. Thank you, Michael. If they had judged by speed I might have come home unbearable, and the house has had enough of me for one noon.

speaker: michael_drayton
text: You would have been unbearable for an afternoon, and then you would have wanted a play again. God keep you. I am taking the long way back, now that the rent is no longer chasing you.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: God keep you, Master Drayton. Mind the kennel. Master Shakespeare, the minute is up.
